title: The Longest Road in a Tree

concept.title: The longest road bends at some node: left height plus right height
body: The **diameter** of a tree is the number of edges on the longest road between any two nodes. The road does not have to pass through the root. Every road has a **highest node** where it turns (it goes down to the left and down to the right from there). The longest road that turns at a node `v` has the length `height(left of v) + height(right of v)` (heights counted as the number of nodes on the longest downward road, so that the sum is the number of edges). The diameter is the best value over all nodes.

body.code:
best = 0

def height(node):                          # number of nodes on the longest downward road
    global best
    if node is None:
        return 0
    left = height(node.left)
    right = height(node.right)
    best = max(best, left + right)         # the road that bends at this node
    return 1 + max(left, right)

height(root)
print(best)

body: The same function computes two things at once: it **returns** the height to its parent, and it **records** the best road bending here in an outside variable. This "return one thing, update another" pattern appears in many tree problems (maximum path sum, longest streak, and so on).

statement: The diameter of a binary tree is the number of edges on the longest path between any two nodes of the tree. The path does not have to pass through the root. Print the diameter.
inputFormat: The first line has `t`, the number of words in the description of the tree.
The second line has the tree in level order: the root first, then the children of the nodes row by row from left to right. `N` stands for a missing child. There is no `N` at the end.
constraints: The height of the tree is at most 800.
hints: Every path turns at its highest node.
The longest path turning at a node is the height of its left subtree plus the height of its right subtree.
Compute heights bottom-up and keep the best sum in a variable that all calls can change.

explanation: A post-order pass returns the height of every subtree and records, at each node, the length (left height + right height) of the longest path that bends there; the diameter is the largest recorded value.

            queue.append(node.left)
        i += 1

            queue.append(node.right)
        i += 1

# Prints a tree in the same level-order form ("empty" for no tree).
def print_tree(root):

        return
    out = []

    head = 0

        node = queue[head]

            queue.append(node.left)
            queue.append(node.right)
    while out and out[-1] == "N":
        out.pop()
    print(" ".join(out))


def diameter(root):
    best = [0]

    def height(node):
        if node is None:
            return 0
        left = height(node.left)
        right = height(node.right)
        best[0] = max(best[0], left + right)
